     1→# Deployment Issues Report
     2→
     3→**Date:** 2026-02-26 to 2026-02-27
     4→**Branch:** `feat/revised-prompts` (deployed from `feat/amazing-hoover` worktree)
     5→**Services:** API (`api`) and Frontend (`frontend`) on GCP Cloud Run (`europe-west4`)
     6→
     7→---
     8→
     9→## Overview
    10→
    11→This report documents all deployment issues encountered while merging the popup OAuth flow from `feat/flamboyant-pasteur` into `feat/revised-prompts` and deploying the API and frontend to GCP Cloud Run.
    12→
    13→---
    14→
    15→## Issue 1: Merge Conflicts (LoginPage.tsx, auth.py)
    16→
    17→**Status:** RESOLVED
    18→
    19→**Problem:** Merging `feat/flamboyant-pasteur` (popup OAuth flow) into `feat/revised-prompts` caused conflicts in:
    20→- `apps/hitl-ui/src/screens/LoginPage.tsx`
    21→- `services/api-service/src/api_service/auth.py`
    22→
    23→**Fix:** Resolved by taking the flamboyant-pasteur popup approach. Added `login` to `useAuth()` destructuring in LoginPage. The popup flow uses `window.open()` + `postMessage` instead of full-page redirect.
    24→
    25→**Files Modified:**
    26→- `apps/hitl-ui/src/screens/LoginPage.tsx` — popup-based login with `popupBlocked` state, `cleanupRef`
    27→- `apps/hitl-ui/src/stores/authStore.ts` — `initiateLogin()` returns `{ popupBlocked, cleanup }`
    28→- `services/api-service/src/api_service/auth.py` — callback returns HTML with `postMessage` to opener
    29→
    30→---
    31→
    32→## Issue 2: Google OAuth "Not Configured" (Missing Env Vars)
    33→
    34→**Status:** RESOLVED
    35→
    36→**Error:**
    37→```json
    38→{"detail":"Google OAuth is not configured. Set GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, or use Dev Login."}
    39→```
    40→
    41→**Root Cause:** `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` were not included in the `deploy_api.sh` script's `--set-env-vars`.
    42→
    43→**Fix:** Added both variables to the `--set-env-vars` in the deploy script and sourced them from `.env`.
    44→
    45→**Files Modified:**
    46→- `scripts/deploy_api.sh` — added `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` to env vars
    47→
    48→---
    49→
    50→## Issue 3: OAuth `redirect_uri_mismatch` (HTTP vs HTTPS)
    51→
    52→**Status:** RESOLVED
    53→
    54→**Error:** Google OAuth returned `redirect_uri_mismatch` because the callback URL was `http://` instead of `https://`.
    55→
    56→**Root Cause:** Cloud Run terminates TLS at its load balancer, so Starlette sees the request as HTTP. `request.url_for("auth_callback")` generated an `http://` URL, which didn't match the registered OAuth redirect URI.
    57→
    58→**Fix:** Added `ProxyHeadersMiddleware` from uvicorn to trust `X-Forwarded-Proto` headers from Cloud Run's load balancer.
    59→
    60→**Files Modified:**
    61→- `services/api-service/src/api_service/main.py`:
    62→  ```python
    63→  from uvicorn.middleware.proxy_headers import ProxyHeadersMiddleware
    64→  app.add_middleware(ProxyHeadersMiddleware, trusted_hosts="*")
    65→  ```
    66→
    67→---
    68→
    69→## Issue 4: CORS Errors on Protocol Upload (Multiple Causes)
    70→
    71→**Status:** RESOLVED
    72→
    73→**Error:**
    74→```
    75→Access to fetch at '.../protocols/upload' from origin 'https://frontend-...' has been blocked by CORS policy
    76→POST .../protocols/upload net::ERR_FAILED 500
    77→```
    78→
    79→### Sub-issue 4a: `--set-env-vars` Delimiter Breaking CORS_ORIGINS
    80→
    81→**Root Cause:** The deploy script used the default comma delimiter for `--set-env-vars`, which broke `CORS_ORIGINS` parsing when it contained multiple comma-separated URLs.
    82→
    83→**Fix:** Switched to `^||^` delimiter syntax:
    84→```bash
    85→--set-env-vars "^||^KEY1=val1||KEY2=val2||CORS_ORIGINS=url1,url2"
    86→```
    87→
    88→### Sub-issue 4b: Only One Frontend URL in CORS
    89→
    90→**Root Cause:** `CORS_ORIGINS` only contained one frontend URL, but there were two (the new-style and legacy Cloud Run URLs).
    91→
    92→**Fix:** Added both frontend URLs:
    93→```
    94→https://frontend-1074735463071.europe-west4.run.app,https://frontend-aq2dyw3nxq-ez.a.run.app
    95→```
    96→
    97→### Sub-issue 4c: 500 Errors Masking CORS
    98→
    99→**Root Cause:** The actual upload endpoint was returning 500 (due to GCS signing issues, see Issue 5). When the server errors before the CORS middleware adds headers, the browser reports it as a CORS error.
   100→
   101→**Fix:** Resolved by fixing the underlying GCS signed URL issue (Issue 5).
   102→
   103→**Files Modified:**
   104→- `scripts/deploy_api.sh` — `^||^` delimiter, both frontend URLs
   105→- `.env` — `FRONTEND_URL` with both URLs
   106→
   107→---
   108→
   109→## Issue 5: GCS Signed URL Generation Failing on Cloud Run
   110→
   111→**Status:** RESOLVED (after 5 iterations)
   112→
   113→**Error:**
   114→```
   115→need a private key to sign credentials
   116→```
   117→
   118→**Root Cause:** Cloud Run uses Compute Engine default credentials, which cannot sign URLs locally (unlike service account JSON key files). The `blob.generate_signed_url()` method requires either a private key or delegation to the IAM `signBlob` API.
   119→
   120→### Iteration 1: Pass `service_account_email` + `client._credentials.token`
   121→**Result:** Failed — token was `None` (lazy-loaded, not yet refreshed).
   122→
   123→### Iteration 2: Refresh credentials first
   124→**Result:** Failed — `_get_signing_kwargs` returned empty dict because `hasattr(credentials, "service_account_email")` check failed on Compute Engine credentials.
   125→
   126→### Iteration 3: `isinstance(Signing)` check + `with_scopes_if_required`
   127→**Result:** Failed — `ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT`. The default Compute Engine credentials didn't have `cloud-platform` scope.
   128→
   129→### Iteration 4: Create new `ce_creds.Credentials` with `cloud-platform` scope
   130→**Result:** Failed — Service account email was `"default"` (not the real email), which the IAM signBlob API rejected.
   131→
   132→### Iteration 5 (Final Fix): Query metadata server for real SA email
   133→**Result:** SUCCESS
   134→
   135→**Final Solution:**
   136→1. Query `http://metadata.google.internal/.../email` for the real SA email
   137→2. Create `google.auth.compute_engine.Credentials` with `cloud-platform` scope
   138→3. Refresh the scoped credentials
   139→4. Pass `service_account_email` and `access_token` to `generate_signed_url()`
   140→
   141→**IAM Prerequisite:** Granted `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` to the compute SA:
   142→```bash
   143→gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding PROJECT \
   144→  --member="serviceAccount:COMPUTE_SA@developer.gserviceaccount.com" \
   145→  --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"
   146→```
   147→
   148→**Files Created:**
   149→- `services/api-service/src/api_service/_gcs_signing.py` — metadata server SA email resolution + scoped credentials
   150→
   151→**Files Modified:**
   152→- `services/api-service/src/api_service/gcs.py` — delegates signing to `_gcs_signing.get_signing_kwargs()`
   153→
   154→---
   155→
   156→## Issue 6: GCS Bucket CORS Missing (Browser-to-GCS PUT)
   157→
   158→**Status:** RESOLVED
   159→
   160→**Error:**
   161→```
   162→Access to fetch at 'https://storage.googleapis.com/medgemma-hackathon-protocols/...' blocked by CORS policy
   163→PUT https://storage.googleapis.com/... net::ERR_FAILED
   164→```
   165→
   166→**Root Cause:** The GCS bucket `medgemma-hackathon-protocols` had no CORS configuration, so the browser's direct PUT upload (using signed URL) was blocked.
   167→
   168→**Fix:** Applied CORS configuration to the bucket:
   169→```bash
   170→gsutil cors set cors.json gs://medgemma-hackathon-protocols
   171→```
   172→With a JSON config allowing both frontend origins for PUT and GET methods.
   173→
   174→---
   175→
   176→## Issue 7: Wrong GCS Bucket Name in Deploy
   177→
   178→**Status:** RESOLVED
   179→
   180→**Error:** Uploads were going to `gen-lang-client-0249847738_cloudbuild` (the Cloud Build staging bucket) instead of `medgemma-hackathon-protocols`.
   181→
   182→**Root Cause:** The deploy script sourced `.env` which had `REDACTED` (for local dev).
   183→
   184→**Fix:** Added `GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PROD` override variable in `.env` and the deploy script:
   185→```bash
   186→GCS_BUCKET_NAME="${GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PROD:-${GCS_BUCKET_NAME:-${PROJECT_ID}-api-protocols}}"
   187→```
   188→
   189→**Files Modified:**

   195→## Issue 8: Protocol Processing → Dead Letter (Missing MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI)
   196→
   197→**Status:** PARTIALLY RESOLVED (see Issue 9)
   198→
   199→**Symptom:** Protocol uploads succeeded (file reached GCS, quality score 82%, 11 pages, 100% text extractable) but immediately became "Dead Letter" with "Processing Failed (Retries Exhausted)".
   200→
   201→**Root Cause:** The protocol processing pipeline runs a `_preflight_check()` before starting. This check requires `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` to be set and the MLflow server to be reachable. Neither condition was met:
   202→1. `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` was not passed in the deploy script's `--set-env-vars`
   203→2. Even when added, the MLflow Cloud Run service requires IAM authentication
   204→
   205→**Fix (partial):**
   206→1. Added `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` to deploy script (auto-resolved from Cloud Run)
   207→2. Granted `roles/run.invoker` to the API's SA on the MLflow service
   208→3. Created `_cloud_run_auth.py` to fetch ID tokens from metadata server and set `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN`
   209→
   210→**Files Created:**
   211→- `services/api-service/src/api_service/_cloud_run_auth.py` — Cloud Run service-to-service auth helper
   212→
   213→**Files Modified:**
   214→- `scripts/deploy_api.sh` — auto-resolve and pass `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`
   215→- `services/api-service/src/api_service/main.py` — call `configure_mlflow_auth()` at startup
   216→- `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/trigger.py` — add Bearer token to preflight health check
   217→
   218→---
   219→
   220→## Issue 9: API Container Fails to Start (OOM + MLflow Cold Start)
   221→
   222→**Status:** PARTIALLY RESOLVED (startup works, MLflow still 503)
   223→
   224→### Sub-issue 9a: Memory Limit Exceeded
   225→
   226→**Error:**
   227→```
   228→Memory limit of 512 MiB exceeded with 554 MiB used
   229→```
   230→
   231→**Root Cause:** The container's 512 MiB default memory was insufficient after adding MLflow + auth dependencies.
   232→
   233→**Fix:** Increased memory to `1Gi` in deploy command (`--memory 1Gi`).
   234→
   235→### Sub-issue 9b: MLflow Cold Start Blocking API Startup
   236→
   237→**Error:** Startup probe timeout — `_init_mlflow()` blocked waiting for the MLflow Cloud Run service to cold-start (30+ seconds).
   238→
   239→**Root Cause:** `_init_mlflow()` makes synchronous HTTP calls to MLflow (`get_experiment`, `set_experiment`) during FastAPI's `lifespan()`. If MLflow is cold-starting, these calls hang for 30+ seconds, exceeding the Cloud Run startup probe deadline.
   240→
   241→**Fix:** Moved `_init_mlflow()` to a background daemon thread so it doesn't block startup:
   242→```python
   243→mlflow_thread = threading.Thread(
   244→    target=_deferred_mlflow_init, daemon=True, name="mlflow-init"
   245→)
   246→mlflow_thread.start()
   247→```
   248→
   249→**Result:** API starts successfully. However, the MLflow init thread eventually fails with:
   250→```
   251→503 error responses from mlflow-....europe-west4.run.app
   252→```
   253→This suggests the MLflow service itself is unhealthy or not properly configured to accept authenticated requests.
   254→
   255→### Sub-issue 9c: MLflow Service Returns 403/503
   256→
   257→**Error:**
   258→```
   259→API request to .../api/3.0/mlflow/traces failed with error code 403
   260→API request to .../api/2.0/mlflow/experiments/get-by-name failed with 503
   261→```
   262→
   263→**Root Cause:** Despite setting `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` with an ID token, the MLflow service still rejects requests. Possible causes:
   264→- MLflow doesn't natively support Cloud Run ID tokens (it uses `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` as a Bearer token, but may expect a different token format)
   265→- The MLflow service itself may be unhealthy (returning 503)
   266→- Organization policy prevents `allUsers` access, so unauthenticated fallback is not possible
   267→
   268→**Status:** UNRESOLVED — The MLflow Cloud Run service needs investigation:
   269→1. Is the MLflow service healthy and properly configured?
   270→2. Does it accept Bearer tokens from Cloud Run ID tokens?
   271→3. Does it need its own database/storage configuration?
   272→
   273→---
   274→
   275→## Issue 10: API Becomes Unresponsive
   276→
   277→**Status:** UNRESOLVED
   278→
   279→**Symptom:** After deploying revision `api-00037-l4j`, the API initially responded (health check returned 200, login redirects worked) but later became completely unresponsive (60s timeout on `/health`).
   280→
   281→**Possible Root Causes:**
   282→- MLflow trace export attempts on every request are returning 503, which may be consuming connections/threads
   283→- The instance may have scaled down and new instances can't start due to lingering issues
   284→- The deferred MLflow init thread may be holding resources
   285→
   286→**Current State:** Login page shows but OAuth callback doesn't reach the API. Health endpoint times out. The API was last confirmed working briefly after the `api-00037-l4j` deployment.
   287→
   288→---
   289→
   290→## Summary of Files Created/Modified
   291→
   292→### New Files
   293→| File | Purpose |
   294→|------|---------|
   295→| `services/api-service/src/api_service/_gcs_signing.py` | GCS signed URL generation on Cloud Run (metadata server SA email + scoped credentials) |
   296→| `services/api-service/src/api_service/_cloud_run_auth.py` | Cloud Run service-to-service auth (ID token fetch for MLflow) |
   297→| `scripts/deploy_api.sh` | API deploy script (moved from `instructions/`) |
   298→| `scripts/deploy_frontend.sh` | Frontend deploy script (moved from `instructions/`) |
   299→
   300→### Modified Files
   301→| File | Changes |
   302→|------|---------|
   303→| `services/api-service/src/api_service/main.py` | Added `ProxyHeadersMiddleware`, Cloud Run MLflow auth, deferred MLflow init thread |
   304→| `services/api-service/src/api_service/auth.py` | Popup OAuth flow (postMessage), explicit client_id/client_secret in OAuth registration |
   305→| `services/api-service/src/api_service/gcs.py` | Delegates signing to `_gcs_signing` module |
   306→| `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/trigger.py` | Bearer token in preflight MLflow health check |
   307→| `apps/hitl-ui/src/screens/LoginPage.tsx` | Popup-based login flow |
   308→| `apps/hitl-ui/src/stores/authStore.ts` | `initiateLogin()` with popup support |
   309→| `Makefile` | Added `deploy-api` and `deploy-frontend` targets |
   310→| `.env` | Added OAuth credentials, `GCS_BUCKET_NAME_PROD`, `FRONTEND_URL` |
   311→
   312→---
   313→
   314→## Current Blocking Issues (Priority Order)
   315→
   316→1. **MLflow service unhealthy (503)** — Root cause of dead-letter processing AND contributes to API instability. Needs direct investigation of the MLflow Cloud Run service.
   317→2. **API unresponsive** — May be caused by MLflow connection storms. Consider disabling MLflow trace export until the service is fixed.
   318→3. **Protocol processing dead-letter** — Blocked by MLflow preflight check. Cannot process protocols until MLflow is reachable.
   319→
   320→## Recommended Next Steps
   321→
   322→1. **Investigate MLflow Cloud Run service** — Check its logs, database connectivity, and whether it's actually running properly
   323→2. **Consider making MLflow preflight optional** — Allow protocol processing to proceed without MLflow tracing as a temporary workaround
   324→3. **Add min-instances=1 to MLflow** — Eliminate cold-start delays: `gcloud run services update mlflow --min-instances 1`
   325→4. **Disable MLflow autolog trace export** — The per-request trace export to a broken MLflow is generating constant 503 errors and may be degrading API performance
   326→

     1→# Architecture
     2→
     3→**Analysis Date:** 2026-02-27
     4→
     5→## Pattern Overview
     6→
     7→**Overall:** Event-driven, multi-service pipeline with distributed LangGraph workflow for clinical trial criteria processing
     8→
     9→**Key Characteristics:**
    10→- **Microservices with shared data layer**: FastAPI gateway (api-service) orchestrates async event processing via PostgreSQL outbox
    11→- **7-node LangGraph pipeline**: Stateful workflow with checkpointing and fault-tolerance for document-to-extraction transformation
    12→- **MedGemma + Gemini multi-model system**: Domain-specific medical reasoning (MedGemma 4B-IT) paired with fast structured extraction (Gemini 2.5 Flash)
    13→- **Terminology grounding with dual validation**: TerminologyRouter + OMOP CDM reconciliation for medical entity concept mapping
    14→- **Human-in-the-loop review**: Final clinician approval gate with edit/approve/reject capabilities
    15→
    16→## Layers
    17→
    18→**Presentation Layer:**
    19→- Purpose: React single-page application for clinician review and approval of extracted criteria
    20→- Location: `apps/hitl-ui/src/`
    21→- Contains: React components, screens, hooks, stores (Zustand), API client
    22→- Depends on: api-service REST API
    23→- Used by: End users (clinicians) for criteria review and export
    24→
    25→**API Service (FastAPI):**
    26→- Purpose: RESTful gateway for protocol uploads, criteria review, exports, and system health
    27→- Location: `services/api-service/src/api_service/`
    28→- Contains: Route handlers (`protocols.py`, `reviews.py`, `exports.py`, `entities.py`), data models, GCS integration, terminology search
    29→- Depends on: PostgreSQL, GCS, shared models library, outbox event system
    30→- Used by: hitl-ui frontend, external clients, internal event handlers
    31→
    32→**Data Persistence Layer:**
    33→- Purpose: PostgreSQL database with SQLModel ORM for all application state
    34→- Location: Schema defined in `services/api-service/alembic/versions/`
    35→- Contains: Protocol, CriteriaBatch, Criteria, Entity, Review, AuditLog, Expression tree tables
    36→- Accessed by: api-service, protocol-processor via SQLModel Session
    37→- Outbox pattern: TransactionalOutbox table for reliable event publishing
    38→
    39→**Protocol Processor Service (LangGraph):**
    40→- Purpose: Async 7-node workflow for PDF ingest, extraction, grounding, and structuring
    41→- Location: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/`
    42→- Contains: StateGraph definition, 7 nodes, tools (extraction, grounding, terminology routing), schemas
    43→- Depends on: PostgreSQL checkpointer, MedGemma (Vertex AI or local), Gemini API, UMLS, OMOP CDM
    44→- Used by: Outbox processor (triggered by ProtocolUploaded events)
    45→
    46→**Shared Libraries:**
    47→- Purpose: Cross-service domain models and utilities
    48→- Location: `libs/shared/`, `libs/inference/`, `libs/events-py/`, etc.
    49→- Contains:
    50→  - `shared/models.py`: SQLModel domain models (Protocol, Criteria, Entity, etc.)
    51→  - `inference/`: MedGemma loading and inference (Vertex AI + local GPU)
    52→  - `events-py/`: Transactional outbox pattern, domain event enums
    53→  - `evaluation/`: Quality assessment frameworks
    54→
    55→## Data Flow
    56→
    57→**Protocol Ingestion → Extraction → Grounding → Review → Export:**
    58→
    59→1. **Upload Phase** (Frontend → API)
    60→   - User uploads PDF to signed GCS URL (direct browser-to-cloud)
    61→   - `POST /protocols/confirm-upload` creates Protocol record + quality metadata
    62→   - Quality score computed via Gemini (page complexity analysis)
    63→   - ProtocolUploaded event persisted in outbox
    64→
    65→2. **Extraction Phase** (Outbox → LangGraph ingest/extract nodes)
    66→   - Outbox processor fetches ProtocolUploaded event
    67→   - Calls `handle_protocol_uploaded()` which invokes LangGraph graph
    68→   - **Ingest node**: Downloads PDF from GCS, validates file format
    69→   - **Extract node**: Calls Gemini File API with structured output schema → JSON criteria with confidence
    70→   - State flow: `protocol_id` + `file_uri` → `pdf_bytes` → `extraction_json`
    71→
    72→3. **Parsing Phase** (Parse node)
    73→   - Parses extraction_json into ExtractionResult Pydantic model
    74→   - Creates CriteriaBatch and Criteria records in PostgreSQL
    75→   - Decomposes criteria text into entities using MedGemma (entity_decomposer.py)
    76→   - Fallback entity type detection by category if decomposition fails
    77→   - State flow: `extraction_json` → `batch_id`, `entities_json`
    78→   - PDF bytes cleared from state to reduce checkpointing size
    79→
    80→4. **Grounding Phase** (Ground node - most complex)
    81→   - For each entity in entities_json:
    82→     a. **TerminologyRouter**: Route to correct UMLS/SNOMED/LOINC/RxNorm/ICD-10/HPO API based on entity_type
    83→     b. **Candidate collection**: Get terminology candidates from ToolUniverse SDK
    84→     c. **MedGemma decision**: LLM selects best candidate + confidence + reasoning
    85→     d. **Agentic retry loop** (if confidence < 0.5):
    86→        - Q1: Is this a valid medical criterion?
    87→        - Q2: Is this a derived entity mapping to a standard concept?
    88→        - Q3: Can entity be rephrased for better search?
    89→        - Max 3 attempts before expert_review routing
    90→     e. **OMOP dual grounding**: Parallel OMOP CDM lookup (lookup_omop_concept)
    91→     f. **Reconciliation**: Compare ToolUniverse + OMOP results via fuzzy matching (≥80% token_set_ratio)
    92→     g. **Audit logging**: Record all MedGemma decisions, candidates considered, reasoning
    93→   - Field mappings generated (entity decomposition path) for AutoCriteria
    94→   - State flow: `entities_json` → `grounded_entities_json`, accumulated errors
    95→
    96→5. **Persistence Phase** (Persist node)
    97→   - Commits Entity DB records with grounding results
    98→   - Maps grounding codes to Entity fields (umls_cui, snomed_code, rxnorm_code, etc.)
    99→   - Sets grounding_method based on confidence (terminology_router_medgemma vs expert_review)
   100→   - Updates Protocol status to "pending_review" (partial success) or "grounding_failed" (total failure)
   101→   - Preserves field_mappings in Criteria.conditions JSONB
   102→   - State flow: `grounded_entities_json` → database commits
   103→
   104→6. **Structuring Phase** (Structure node)
   105→   - Builds expression trees from criteria text (AND/OR/NOT logic)
   106→   - Creates ExpressionTree, ExpressionNode, ExpressionEdge records
   107→   - Uses structure_builder.py tool for tree decomposition
   108→   - State flow: persisted Criteria → ExpressionTree records
   109→
   110→7. **Ordinal Resolution Phase** (Ordinal_resolve node)
   111→   - Detects and maps ordinal scales (NYHA, ECOG, Karnofsky, etc.)
   112→   - Normalizes scale values to OMOP unit concepts
   113→   - Proposes ordinal_proposals_json for clinician approval in review interface
   114→   - State flow: Criteria with ordinal text → unit_concept_id mappings
   115→
   116→8. **Review Phase** (API review endpoints)
   117→   - `GET /reviews/batches`: List all batches pending review
   118→   - `GET /reviews/batches/{batch_id}/criteria`: Fetch criteria + entities for batch
   119→   - User sees split-pane UI: original protocol PDF + criteria/entities with grounding
   120→   - `POST /reviews/criteria/{criteria_id}/action`: Clinician submits approve/reject/modify
   121→   - Decisions persisted to Review table + update Criteria status
   122→
   123→9. **Export Phase** (Export endpoints)
   124→   - `GET /exports/{batch_id}/circe`: OHDSI CIRCE JSON for cohort identification
   125→   - `GET /exports/{batch_id}/fhir-group`: FHIR R4 Group resource
   126→   - `GET /exports/{batch_id}/evaluation-sql`: OMOP CDM evaluation SQL
   127→   - Exporters in `services/api-service/src/api_service/exporters/`
   128→
   129→**State Management:**
   130→- **LangGraph State** (PipelineState TypedDict): Minimal flat structure with JSON strings for complex objects to reduce token usage during checkpointing
   131→- **Database State** (SQLModel): All persistent application state (protocols, criteria, entities, audit logs)
   132→- **Checkpoint State** (AsyncPostgresSaver): LangGraph checkpoints persisted to PostgreSQL for fault-tolerance; thread_id = protocol_id:uuid4 to prevent collision on re-extraction
   133→
   134→## Key Abstractions
   135→
   136→**PipelineState (LangGraph):**
   137→- Purpose: Minimal state vector passed between 7 nodes
   138→- Examples: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/state.py`
   139→- Pattern: TypedDict with on-demand population; complex data stored as JSON strings; pdf_bytes cleared after extract node
   140→
   141→**TerminologyRouter:**
   142→- Purpose: Entity-type-aware UMLS/SNOMED/LOINC/RxNorm/ICD-10/HPO API routing
   143→- Examples: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/tools/terminology_router.py`
   144→- Pattern: YAML config-driven routing; singleton instance; caches lookups; returns GroundingCandidate objects
   145→
   146→**EntityGroundingResult:**
   147→- Purpose: Result of MedGemma-selected terminology match
   148→- Examples: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/schemas/grounding.py`
   149→- Pattern: Pydantic model with code, system, confidence, reasoning, selected_code, agentic_attempt_count, reconciliation_status
   150→
   151→**AgenticReasoningLoop:**
   152→- Purpose: 3-question retry when MedGemma confidence < 0.5
   153→- Examples: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/tools/medgemma_decider.py` (agentic_reasoning_loop)
   154→- Pattern: Questions reformulated at each iteration; query rephrasing for terminology search; expert_review routing on exhaustion
   155→
   156→**ExpressionTree:**
   157→- Purpose: Structured representation of criteria logic (AND/OR/NOT operations)
   158→- Examples: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/tools/structure_builder.py`
   159→- Pattern: Hierarchical tree nodes with operator types; persisted to database
   160→
   161→## Entry Points
   162→
   163→**API Service Entry:**
   164→- Location: `services/api-service/src/api_service/main.py`
   165→- Triggers: Application startup (lifespan context manager)
   166→- Responsibilities: Initialize FastAPI app, register routers (protocols, reviews, exports, auth), setup CORS, middleware (MLflow tracing), outbox processor
   167→
   168→**Protocol Upload Trigger:**
   169→- Location: `POST /protocols/confirm-upload` in `services/api-service/src/api_service/protocols.py`
   170→- Triggers: User confirms file upload
   171→- Responsibilities: Create Protocol record, compute quality score, emit ProtocolUploaded event to outbox
   172→
   173→**Outbox Event Handler:**
   174→- Location: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/trigger.py` (handle_protocol_uploaded)
   175→- Triggers: OutboxProcessor polls ProtocolUploaded events
   176→- Responsibilities: Invoke LangGraph graph with thread_id = protocol_id:unique_id, handle async execution, MLflow tracing setup
   177→
   178→**Frontend Entry:**
   179→- Location: `apps/hitl-ui/src/main.tsx`
   180→- Triggers: Browser loads http://localhost:3000 (or production URL)
   181→- Responsibilities: Initialize React app, Zustand store (review UI state), connect to API at /api
   182→
   183→## Error Handling
   184→
   185→**Strategy:** Multi-layered with partial success preservation and expert review escalation
   186→
   187→**Patterns:**
   188→
   189→1. **Fatal vs. Non-Fatal Errors:**
   190→   - **Fatal** (stops pipeline): ingest/extract/parse failures → conditional edge to END
   191→   - **Non-fatal** (continues pipeline): Individual entity grounding failures → accumulated in state.errors list, entities routed to expert_review
   192→
   193→2. **Checkpoint Recovery:**
   194→   - LangGraph persists state after each node to AsyncPostgresSaver
   195→   - `POST /protocols/{protocol_id}/retry` resumes from last successful checkpoint
   196→   - Thread ID stored in protocol.metadata_ to prevent collision on re-extraction
   197→
   198→3. **Agentic Retry:**
   199→   - MedGemma confidence < 0.5 → 3-question retry loop
   200→   - Q1 (validity), Q2 (derivation), Q3 (rephrasing) with query optimization
   201→   - If all attempts fail → expert_review routing (AuditLog + manual clinician review)
   202→
   203→4. **Partial Success Handling:**
   204→   - Some entities grounded successfully + some failed → Protocol status "pending_review"
   205→   - All entities failed → Protocol status "grounding_failed"
   206→   - Clinicians see both successes and failures in review interface with clear indicators
   207→
   208→5. **API Error Responses:**
   209→   - HTTPException with proper status codes (400 bad request, 404 not found, 500 server error)
   210→   - Details logged to server logs + MLflow traces for debugging
   211→   - Outbox events NOT published on extract/parse/ingest failures (no cascading retries)
   212→
   213→6. **Terminology Service Failures:**
   214→   - UMLS/SNOMED timeout → fallback to OMOP or expert_review
   215→   - MedGemma unavailable → expert_review routing
   216→   - Gemini API rate limit → automatic retry with backoff (handled by gemini_breaker in resilience.py)
   217→
   218→## Cross-Cutting Concerns
   219→
   220→**Logging:**
   221→- Framework: Python logging module with structured logging via MLflow spans
   222→- Approach: Each LangGraph node emits pipeline_span() to MLflow; AuditLog table captures grounding decisions; full audit trail per user requirement
   223→
   224→**Validation:**
   225→- PDF validation: file format + page count in ingest node
   226→- Extraction validation: ExtractionResult Pydantic model validates JSON structure
   227→- Entity validation: entity_type must be one of [Condition, Lab_Value, Medication, Procedure, Demographic, Device, Symptom, Consent]
   228→- Grounding validation: confidence >= 0.7 considered high confidence; < 0.5 triggers agentic retry
   229→
   230→**Authentication:**
   231→- API auth: `api_service/auth.py` with optional bearer token validation (can be disabled for local dev)
   232→- OAuth2/OIDC integration for production deployments (via cloud_run_auth.py for GCP Cloud Run)
   233→
   234→**Tracing & Observability:**
   235→- MLflow experiment per day (protocol-processing-YYYYMMDD)
   236→- Each node creates pipeline_span() with inputs/outputs
   237→- Traces stream in real-time (no end-of-pipeline blocking)
   238→- Cleanup of orphaned IN_PROGRESS traces at startup (fallback from crashes)
   239→
   240→**Configuration:**
   241→- Environment variables: GOOGLE_API_KEY, UMLS_API_KEY, MODEL_BACKEND (vertex|local), DATABASE_URL, MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI
   242→- Singleton patterns: TerminologyRouter, LangGraph graph, OmopClient loaded once at first use
   243→- Service discovery: Hardcoded URLs for Vertex AI, local GPU via environment variables
   244→
   245→---
   246→
   247→*Architecture analysis: 2026-02-27*
   248→
```

## RESEARCH COMPLETE

**Project:** MedGemma Cloud Run Deployment Reliability
**Mode:** Architecture dimension (ecosystem research)
**Confidence:** HIGH

### Key Findings

- **MLflow is hardcoded as a required dependency in 3 locations** (`_preflight_check()`, `_cleanup_orphan_traces()` at module scope, `_ensure_mlflow()`) despite being observability tooling. This is the root cause of all three stated problems.
- **The codebase already has a circuit breaker pattern** (`pybreaker` in `shared/resilience.py`) for Gemini, GCS, Vertex AI, and ToolUniverse -- but not for MLflow. Adding an `mlflow_breaker` is a minimal-diff fix.
- **The `/health` endpoint is already correctly designed** -- it only fails on PostgreSQL unavailability and treats OMOP/GCS/breakers as informational. This makes it suitable for Cloud Run startup/liveness probes as-is.
- **MLflow version mismatch**: Cloud Run Dockerfile uses v2.19.0, docker-compose uses v3.9.0. The production deployment lacks async logging available in v3.x.
- **Security gap**: MLflow Cloud Run is deployed with `--allow-unauthenticated` while the `_cloud_run_auth.py` module already implements ID token acquisition for authenticated calls.

### Files Created

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `/Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/.planning/research/ARCHITECTURE.md` | System structure, component boundaries, dependency classification, degradation patterns, build order |

### Confidence Assessment

| Area | Level | Reason |
|------|-------|--------|
| Component boundaries | HIGH | Direct codebase analysis of all service files |
| Dependency classification | HIGH | Code-level evidence of where MLflow blocks pipeline |
| Circuit breaker pattern | HIGH | Extends existing `pybreaker` infrastructure already in the project |
| Cloud Run probe config | MEDIUM | Official docs verified; exact CLI flags should be confirmed at deploy time |
| MLflow async logging | MEDIUM | Confirmed in MLflow docs but version mismatch (v2.19 vs v3.x) needs resolution |

### Roadmap Implications

**Phase 1 (Decouple MLflow)** should be first -- it resolves all three stated problems with minimal code changes and no infrastructure work. It involves: adding `mlflow_breaker` to `resilience.py`, removing MLflow from `_preflight_check()`, moving `_cleanup_orphan_traces()` out of module scope, and wrapping `pipeline_span()`/`llm_span()` with circuit breaker fallback.

**Phase 2 (Service Auth)** and **Phase 3 (Health Probes)** can be done in parallel after Phase 1.

**Phase 4 (Version Alignment)** depends on Phase 1 being in place -- async logging helps but does not replace circuit breaking.

### Open Questions

- What is the actual production MLflow version? The Dockerfile says v2.19.0 but docker-compose says v3.9.0. This determines whether async logging env vars are available.
- Should MLflow be behind IAM authentication? The `_cloud_run_auth.py` module exists but MLflow is deployed with `--allow-unauthenticated`. This is a security decision that affects the auth hardening phase.
- What is the acceptable trace data loss rate? If MLflow is down for an hour, all traces from that period are lost. Is this acceptable, or should traces be buffered to disk for later replay?

## RESEARCH COMPLETE

**Project:** MedGemma -- Cloud Run Deployment Reliability
**Mode:** Ecosystem (Stack dimension)
**Confidence:** HIGH

### Key Findings

- **Service-to-service auth fix is straightforward:** Replace raw metadata server HTTP calls in `_cloud_run_auth.py` with `google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token()` from the `google-auth` library (already a transitive dependency). The API service account needs `roles/run.invoker` on the MLflow service.
- **MLflow token refresh works via env var:** MLflow re-reads `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` on every API call (confirmed via resolved GitHub issue #8823). Simply update `os.environ["MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN"]` before MLflow operations using `fetch_id_token()`.
- **MLflow must become optional:** The `_preflight_check()` in `trigger.py` treats MLflow as a hard dependency (`raise DependencyCheckError` if unreachable). This must change to a warning with a `mlflow_required_for_pipeline` configuration flag (default: False).
- **`pydantic-settings` centralizes config:** Replace scattered `os.getenv()` calls with a validated `AppSettings` class. Version 2.13.1 supports GCP Secret Manager natively via extras.
- **No new circuit breaker library needed:** `pybreaker` (already in use, v1.4.1) is correct for this codebase's threading model. Add an `mlflow_breaker` alongside existing Gemini/GCS/Vertex AI breakers.

### Files Created

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `/Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/.planning/research/STACK.md` | Technology recommendations for Cloud Run deployment reliability |

### Confidence Assessment

| Area | Level | Reason |
|------|-------|--------|
| Service-to-service auth | HIGH | Verified via official GCP docs and google-auth library docs |
| MLflow token refresh | HIGH | Confirmed via resolved GitHub issue with maintainer verification |
| Configuration management | HIGH | pydantic-settings is FastAPI's official recommendation, verified on PyPI |
| Circuit breakers | HIGH | pybreaker already in use, verified version on PyPI |
| Structured logging | MEDIUM | structlog version verified, but GCP integration (structlog-gcp) has less community validation |

### Roadmap Implications

1. **Phase 1: Make MLflow optional** -- Change `_preflight_check()` to warn instead of raise. Add `mlflow_breaker` circuit breaker. This alone fixes the dead-lettering problem.
2. **Phase 2: Fix service-to-service auth** -- Replace `_cloud_run_auth.py` with `google.oauth2.id_token.fetch_id_token()`. Ensure IAM binding for `roles/run.invoker`.
3. **Phase 3: Centralize configuration** -- Introduce `pydantic-settings` `AppSettings` class. Add environment-aware defaults and feature flags.
4. **Phase 4: Add timeouts and structured logging** -- Replace `urllib.request.urlopen()` with `httpx.Client`, add Cloud Run startup/liveness probes, optionally add structlog.

### Open Questions

- **MLflow server version mismatch:** The MLflow Docker image is v2.19.0 but the client in dev deps is >=3.8.1. This client-server version gap works for tracking API but should be verified for trace export specifically.
- **`mlflow-tracing` migration:** The lightweight `mlflow-tracing` package (95% smaller) could replace full `mlflow` in production. This requires assessing which MLflow APIs the codebase actually uses in production vs dev-only. Flag for a future milestone.
- **Cloud Run min-instances:** If the MLflow service cold-starts take 30s+, consider setting `--min-instances=1` to avoid cold start latency. This has cost implications that need evaluation.

## RESEARCH COMPLETE

**Project:** MedGemma Cloud Run Deployment Reliability
**Mode:** Ecosystem (Features dimension)
**Confidence:** HIGH

### Key Findings

- **The #1 issue is MLflow blocking protocol processing.** The preflight check in `trigger.py` (`_preflight_check()`) raises `DependencyCheckError` when MLflow is unreachable, which dead-letters the protocol event. MLflow is observability tooling -- it should never block clinical data processing. This is a LOW complexity fix.

- **Token refresh is already mostly implemented.** The `_cloud_run_auth.py` module fetches ID tokens from the metadata server with caching, but `configure_mlflow_auth()` is only called at startup and once during preflight. MLflow reads `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` from the environment on every request (confirmed via [mlflow#8823](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/issues/8823)), so refreshing `os.environ["MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN"]` before pipeline runs is sufficient.

- **No MLflow circuit breaker exists.** The `resilience.py` module has breakers for Gemini, GCS, UMLS, and Vertex AI, but not MLflow. Failed trace exports currently block for the full timeout duration.

- **Deploy scripts use imperative `--set-env-vars` pattern.** Omitting a variable accidentally removes it. The production pattern for Cloud Run is declarative YAML manifests with `gcloud run services replace`.

- **Startup probes are not configured.** Services use Cloud Run's default 240-second startup timeout, which is appropriate but explicit probes improve reliability signaling.

| `/Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/.planning/research/FEATURES.md` | Feature landscape with table stakes, differentiators, anti-features, dependencies, and prioritization |

| Table Stakes | HIGH | Based on direct codebase analysis of the failing code paths + official GCP docs |
| Differentiators | HIGH | Standard Cloud Run production patterns verified with official docs |

| Dependencies | HIGH | Traced through codebase imports and call chains |

### Roadmap Implications

The features naturally split into three phases:

1. **Fix Active Failures (P1):** MLflow as optional dependency, token refresh, health check separation, startup probes. All LOW-MEDIUM complexity. Should unblock all current deployment issues.

2. **Harden Deployment (P2):** Circuit breaker for MLflow, deploy verification, traffic splitting, min instances, CPU boost, liveness probes. All LOW complexity quality-of-life improvements.

3. **Production Hardening (P3):** YAML manifests, dedicated service accounts, structured logging, MLflow auth plugin. Only needed if the deployment grows or faces security audit.

Phase 1 should be done first because it fixes the three active bugs: 403 on MLflow calls, dead-lettered protocols, and API unresponsiveness when MLflow is down.

### Open Questions

- **LangGraph checkpoint storage in production:** Currently using SQLite for checkpoints locally. Cloud Run ephemeral filesystem means checkpoints are lost on restart. Need to verify if PostgreSQL checkpoint store is configured for production.
- **Outbox processor retry behavior:** How many times does the outbox retry before dead-lettering? Is the current retry count appropriate given that MLflow-blocking will be removed?
- **MLflow trace volume:** What is the actual write throughput to MLflow? Determines whether a single instance with max-instances=1 is sufficient or if async batching is needed.

## RESEARCH COMPLETE

**Project:** MedGemma Deployment Fix
**Mode:** Ecosystem (Pitfalls dimension)
**Confidence:** HIGH

### Key Findings

- **Root cause of all three remaining issues is MLflow coupling.** Synchronous trace export blocks the API event loop, the hard preflight check kills protocol processing, and token expiry causes cascading 403s. These are three symptoms of one problem: MLflow was integrated as a hard dependency rather than an optional observability layer.

- **A single environment variable (`MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING=true`) resolves the API unresponsiveness.** MLflow 2.16.0+ supports async trace logging, and the project uses v2.19.0. This is not configured anywhere in the codebase.

- **The preflight check in `trigger.py` conflates observability with infrastructure.** Lines 328-359 treat MLflow reachability as equivalent to database reachability. Removing MLflow from the hard check unblocks all protocol processing.

- **Cloud Run's default CPU throttling starves the outbox processor between requests.** The `OutboxProcessor` polls every 1 second in a background asyncio task, but CPU is only allocated during HTTP request processing. Adding `--no-cpu-throttling` is required for the background worker pattern.

- **ID token refresh is a known MLflow limitation.** `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` is static -- MLflow has no built-in token refresh ([FR #8823](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/issues/8823)). The `_cloud_run_auth.py` has refresh logic but it is only called at startup and in preflight, not on the hot path.

| Token expiry (#3) | HIGH | MLflow FR #8823 confirms no built-in refresh; `_cloud_run_auth.py` analysis confirms the gap |
| `--set-secrets` wipe (#4) | HIGH | GCP official docs + project's own DEPLOYMENT.md documents this exact mistake |
| CPU throttling (#5) | HIGH | GCP official docs on billing settings; `--no-cpu-throttling` not present in deploy script |
| Env var delimiter (#6) | HIGH | Already resolved in codebase; documented for completeness |

### Roadmap Implications

**Phase 1 (Immediate -- make it work):**
1. Add `MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING=true` to deploy env vars (fixes API unresponsiveness)
2. Remove MLflow from `_preflight_check()` hard requirements (fixes protocol dead-lettering)
3. Add deploy script validation for required secrets

**Phase 2 (Reliability -- make it robust):**
1. Add `--no-cpu-throttling` to deploy script (fixes outbox processor starvation)
2. Add periodic ID token refresh or deploy MLflow with `--allow-unauthenticated`
3. Add MLflow circuit breaker to request middleware

### Open Questions

- Should MLflow be deployed with `--allow-unauthenticated` (simpler but less secure) or with IAM auth (requires token refresh infrastructure)? This depends on whether clinical data appears in MLflow traces.
- Is the current 1Gi memory sufficient when the outbox processor runs a pipeline concurrently with serving HTTP requests? Monitor memory after enabling `--no-cpu-throttling`.

    14→| **MLflow as optional dependency (not blocking)** | Preflight check in `trigger.py` raises `DependencyCheckError` if MLflow health check fails, which dead-letters the protocol event. Make MLflow tracing best-effort throughout: wrap all MLflow calls in try/except, log warnings, continue processing. The existing `MLflowRequestMiddleware` already does this pattern correctly. |
    15→| **Startup probes for Cloud Run services** | Without startup probes, Cloud Run uses a 240-second default. The `/health` endpoint already exists and checks DB connectivity. |
    16→| **Health check that distinguishes required vs optional deps** | Current `/health` returns 503 if DB is down (correct) but does not distinguish MLflow/OMOP failures. Current `/ready` requires both DB *and* OMOP, which is correct but MLflow is checked nowhere. The real issue: if MLflow is down, the API appears healthy but protocol processing silently fails. | LOW | `/health` should check only hard dependencies (DB). `/ready` should check DB + OMOP. Add a separate `/status` endpoint that reports all dependency states (DB, OMOP, MLflow, GCS, circuit breakers) for operational visibility. Already partially implemented via `_check_breakers()`. |
    17→| **Idempotent deploy scripts** | `deploy_api.sh` uses `--set-env-vars` which replaces all env vars on every deploy. If a variable is accidentally omitted, it disappears. The script exits on first error (`set -e`) but does not validate post-deploy state. | MEDIUM | Use `gcloud run services replace` with a YAML service manifest for declarative, fully-specified deployments. This makes the deploy truly idempotent: the YAML is the source of truth. Pin secret versions (e.g., `db-url:latest` is risky; use `db-url:3`). Add post-deploy verification: check the service URL returns 200 from `/health`. |
    18→| **Environment-aware configuration** | Deploy script sources `.env` and constructs `--set-env-vars` inline. No separate staging environment config exists. | MEDIUM | Use a per-environment YAML manifest (e.g., `deploy/production.yaml`, `deploy/staging.yaml`). The lifespan handler awaits `processor.stop()` then waits for `_running_tasks`, but if the pipeline is mid-execution (Gemini API calls), 10 seconds may not be enough. | MEDIUM | Set `--timeout` (request timeout) and `--termination-grace-period` appropriately in Cloud Run config.     41→| **Cloud Run service mesh / Envoy sidecar** | "Proper" service mesh with automatic mTLS and service discovery | Massive complexity overhead for 3-4 services.     42→| **Multi-region deployment** | High availability across regions | This is a hackathon/clinical trial tool, not a global SaaS product.     43→| **Custom domain with managed SSL** | Professional look with custom domain | Adds DNS management, certificate provisioning complexity.     44→| **Terraform / Pulumi for infrastructure** | Infrastructure as code is "best practice" | For 3-4 services, Terraform adds a dependency (state management, provider versions, plan/apply workflow) without proportional benefit. YAML manifests + deploy scripts are simpler and sufficient. | YAML service manifests versioned in git + shell deploy scripts. Graduate to Terraform only if infrastructure grows beyond 10+ resources. |

Adding Pub/Sub means managing subscriptions, dead-letter topics, and ordering guarantees for minimal benefit when services are co-located in the same region. | Keep the outbox pattern for intra-service async processing. Never block pipeline execution on MLflow availability. |
    47→| **Automatic MLflow scaling** | "MLflow should handle production load" | MLflow tracking server is designed for metadata and light artifact storage, not high-throughput workloads.     88→### Dependency Notes
    89→
    90→- **Service-to-Service Auth requires nothing else first:** The existing `_cloud_run_auth.py` already fetches tokens. The fix is making refresh automatic/periodic, not adding new infrastructure.
    91→- **MLflow as Optional requires Circuit Breaker:** Without a breaker, each failed MLflow call blocks for the timeout duration. The breaker ensures fast-fail after threshold.
    92→- **YAML Manifests enable everything else in the deploy pipeline:** Once manifests exist, traffic splitting, verification, and environment-aware config are straightforward additions.
    93→- **Minimum Instances conflicts with Cost Optimization:** Set min=1 for API (user-facing), min=0 for MLflow and processing (background services).

    95→## MVP Definition
    96→
    97→### Launch With (v1) -- Fix What's Broken
    98→
    99→- [x] **MLflow as optional dependency** -- Remove from preflight checks, wrap all MLflow calls in try/except. This is the #1 fix: protocol processing should never dead-letter because tracing is down.
   100→- [x] **Service-to-service auth token refresh** -- Refresh `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` before each pipeline run (not just at startup). Use the existing `configure_mlflow_auth()` which already refreshes from metadata server.
   101→- [x] **Health check separation** -- `/health` = DB only (required). `/ready` = DB + OMOP (required for full functionality). MLflow state in response body but not blocking.
   102→- [x] **Startup probes** -- Add `--startup-probe` to deploy commands for API and MLflow services.
   103→
   104→### Add After Validation (v1.x) -- Harden the Deployment
   105→
   106→- [ ] **Circuit breaker for MLflow** -- Trigger: MLflow trace exports cause latency spikes. Add `mlflow_breaker` to `resilience.py`.
   107→- [ ] **Deploy verification step** -- Trigger: any deploy that passes but serves errors. Post-deploy health check with auto-rollback.
   108→- [ ] **Traffic splitting** -- Trigger: confidence in safe deployment process. Deploy with `--no-traffic`, verify, shift.
   109→- [ ] **Minimum instances for API** -- Trigger: user complaints about cold start latency. Set `--min-instances=1`.
   110→- [ ] **Startup CPU boost** -- Trigger: same as above. Free to enable, no downside.
   111→- [ ] **Liveness probes** -- Trigger: containers become unresponsive without restarting.
   112→
   113→### Future Consideration (v2+) -- Production Hardening

### Success Criteria Preview

**Phase 1: MLflow Decoupling**
1. A protocol PDF uploaded via the API completes the full 7-node extraction pipeline when MLflow is unreachable (no dead-lettering)
2. The API /health endpoint responds within 2 seconds even when MLflow is returning 503 on every request
3. When MLflow comes back online after being down, tracing resumes automatically without restarting the API
4. Running the full pipeline locally via Docker Compose produces identical results to before these changes (no regressions)

**Phase 2: Service Auth and MLflow Recovery**
1. The API can write trace data to the MLflow Cloud Run service using ID tokens from the metadata server (no 403 errors)
2. After the API has been running for more than 1 hour, MLflow trace exports still succeed (token is refreshed before expiry)

**Phase 3: Deploy Hardening**
1. Running the deploy script with a missing required env var fails immediately with a clear error message (before any gcloud commands)
2. The deployed API container starts successfully under Cloud Run's startup probe without false-positive restarts
3. The outbox background processor continues polling for pending protocols between HTTP requests (CPU not throttled)
4. After deploy completes, the script automatically verifies the new revision is healthy and reports pass/fail

### Coverage

All 12 v1 requirements mapped. No orphaned requirements.

### Phase Rationale

Phase 1 is the critical path -- all three active failures (403/503, API unresponsive, dead-lettered protocols) trace to MLflow being a hard dependency. Local compatibility guards (LOCL-01, LOCL-02) are in Phase 1 because every code change in that phase must be environment-aware. Phase 2 depends on Phase 1 (auth fixes only matter once MLflow is optional). Phase 3 depends on Phase 1 but not Phase 2 (deploy hardening is independent of auth), though executing it last means it benefits from all code changes being in place.

Phase 1 (MLflow Decoupling) is fully complete. Here is the summary of everything accomplished:

---

## Phase 1: MLflow Decoupling -- Complete

**Goal**: Protocol processing and API responsiveness work regardless of MLflow health status.

### Plan 01-01: Circuit Breaker Foundation (3 commits)

| Commit | File | Change |
|--------|------|--------|
| `19b0d76` | `/Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/libs/shared/src/shared/resilience.py` | Added `mlflow_breaker` (fail_max=3, reset_timeout=120s) and `mlflow_is_available()` helper |
| `300e30a` | `/Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/trigger.py` | Converted MLflow preflight from hard `DependencyCheckError` to soft warning; gated `_ensure_mlflow()` and `_cleanup_orphan_traces()` with breaker |
| `ab82861` | `/Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/services/api-service/src/api_service/main.py` | Hardened `_init_mlflow()` with breaker check and breaker trip on failure |

### Plan 01-02: Wire Breaker Into All Call Sites (3 commits)

| Commit | File | Change |
|--------|------|--------|
| `8938408` | `/Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/tracing.py` | `pipeline_span()` and `llm_span()` return no-op spans immediately when breaker is open; span failures trip the breaker |
| `9124b54` | `/Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/services/api-service/src/api_service/middleware.py` and `main.py` | `MLflowRequestMiddleware` skips tracing when breaker is open (zero overhead); `/health` includes `mlflow_available` as informational boolean |
| `5d69126` | `/Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/scripts/deploy_api.sh` and `/Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/infra/docker-compose.yml` | `MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING=true` in both Cloud Run deploy and local docker-compose |

### Success Criteria Verification

1. **Pipeline completes when MLflow is unreachable**: All MLflow call sites (`tracing.py`, `trigger.py`, `main.py`, `middleware.py`) check `mlflow_is_available()` first and fall back to no-ops. No MLflow failure can block the pipeline.

2. **`/health` responds fast when MLflow is down**: The circuit breaker check is a simple string comparison (`str(breaker.current_state) != "open"`). No network calls to MLflow. MLflow status is informational only -- `/health` returns 200 as long as DB is connected.

3. **Tracing resumes when MLflow recovers**: The circuit breaker auto-transitions from OPEN to HALF_OPEN after 120 seconds (`reset_timeout=120`). The next MLflow call attempt succeeds and closes the breaker, resuming tracing.

4. **Local dev unchanged**: Docker-compose still starts MLflow, the breaker starts closed, and tracing works normally. Only addition is `MLFLOW_ENABLE_ASYNC_TRACE_LOGGING=true` for non-blocking trace export.

### Architecture Pattern

All MLflow integration points now follow this pattern:
```python
from shared.resilience import mlflow_breaker, mlflow_is_available

# Fast path: skip when breaker is open
if not mlflow_is_available():
    # return no-op / skip
    return

try:
    # MLflow operation
except Exception:
    # Trip breaker so subsequent calls fast-path
    try:
        mlflow_breaker.open()
    except Exception:
        pass
```

  "roadmap_content": "# Roadmap: MedGemma Deployment Fix

## Overview

All three deployment failures (MLflow 403/503, API unresponsive, dead-lettered protocols) trace to a single root cause: MLflow treated as a hard dependency. Phase 1 decouples MLflow so the pipeline runs regardless of MLflow health. Phase 2 fixes service-to-service auth so MLflow tracing works when MLflow IS available. Phase 3 hardens the deploy script with probes, CPU config, validation, and post-deploy verification. After all three phases, the full protocol upload-to-export pipeline runs reliably on Cloud Run with graceful MLflow degradation.

## Phases

**Phase Numbering:**
- Integer phases (1, 2, 3): Planned milestone work
- Decimal phases (2.1, 2.2): Urgent insertions (marked with INSERTED)

Decimal phases appear between their surrounding integers in numeric order.

- [x] **Phase 1: MLflow Decoupling** - Make MLflow optional so the pipeline and API work regardless of MLflow health
- [ ] **Phase 2: Service Auth and MLflow Recovery** - Fix service-to-service auth so MLflow tracing works when available
- [ ] **Phase 3: Deploy Hardening** - Make deploy script robust, self-verifying, and production-ready

## Phase Details

### Phase 1: MLflow Decoupling
**Goal**: Protocol processing and API responsiveness work regardless of MLflow health status
**Depends on**: Nothing (first phase)
**Requirements**: MLFL-01, MLFL-02, MLFL-03, MLFL-04, LOCL-01, LOCL-02
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
  1. A protocol PDF uploaded via the API completes the full 7-node extraction pipeline when MLflow is unreachable (no dead-lettering)
  2. The API /health endpoint responds within 2 seconds even when MLflow is returning 503 on every request
  3. When MLflow comes back online after being down, tracing resumes automatically without restarting the API
  4. Running the full pipeline locally via Docker Compose produces identical results to before these changes (no regressions)
**Plans**: 2 plans

Plans:
- [x] 01-01-PLAN.md — Add MLflow circuit breaker, convert preflight to soft warning, harden init
- [x] 01-02-PLAN.md — Gate tracing/middleware with breaker, health endpoint, async trace logging config

### Phase 2: Service Auth and MLflow Recovery
**Goal**: MLflow Cloud Run service accepts authenticated requests from the API, and tokens stay fresh across the service lifetime
**Depends on**: Phase 1
**Requirements**: AUTH-01, AUTH-02
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
  1. The API can write trace data to the MLflow Cloud Run service using ID tokens obtained from the metadata server (no 403 errors)
  2. After the API has been running for more than 1 hour, MLflow trace exports still succeed (token is refreshed before expiry)
**Plans**: TBD

Plans:
- [ ] 02-01: TBD

### Phase 3: Deploy Hardening
**Goal**: Deploy script is robust, idempotent, and self-verifying so deployments succeed reliably without manual intervention
**Depends on**: Phase 1
**Requirements**: DEPL-01, DEPL-02, DEPL-03, DEPL-04
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):
  1. Running the deploy script with a missing required env var fails immediately with a clear error message (before any gcloud commands execute)
  2. The deployed API container starts successfully under Cloud Run's startup probe without false-positive restarts
  3. The outbox background processor continues polling for pending protocols between HTTP requests (CPU not throttled)
  4. After deploy completes, the script automatically verifies the new revision is healthy and reports pass/fail
**Plans**: TBD

Plans:
- [ ] 03-01: TBD

## Progress

**Execution Order:**
Phases execute in numeric order: 1 -> 2 -> 3

| Phase | Plans Complete | Status | Completed |
|-------|----------------|--------|-----------|
| 1. MLflow Decoupling | 2/2 | Complete | 2026-02-27 |
| 2. Service Auth and MLflow Recovery | 0/0 | Not started | - |
| 3. Deploy Hardening | 0/0 | Not started | - |
",
  "requirements_content": "# Requirements: MedGemma Deployment Fix

**Defined:** 2026-02-27
**Core Value:** Deployed Cloud Run services handle the full protocol pipeline end-to-end, exactly as locally

## v1 Requirements

Requirements for getting the deployment working and stable. Each maps to roadmap phases.

### MLflow Decoupling

- [ ] **MLFL-01**: Protocol processing completes successfully when MLflow is unreachable (preflight check warns instead of raising)
- [ ] **MLFL-02**: API remains responsive when MLflow trace export returns 503 (async trace logging enabled)
- [ ] **MLFL-03**: MLflow tracing works when MLflow IS available (no-op fallback does not permanently disable tracing)
- [ ] **MLFL-04**: Circuit breaker added for MLflow client operations (fast-fail after threshold, auto-recover when healthy)

### Service Auth

- [ ] **AUTH-01**: MLflow Cloud Run service accepts authenticated requests from API service (ID token via metadata server)
- [ ] **AUTH-02**: MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN is refreshed before each pipeline run (not just at startup)

### Deploy Reliability

- [ ] **DEPL-01**: Deploy script includes startup probe configuration for API service
- [ ] **DEPL-02**: Deploy script includes --no-cpu-throttling for background outbox processor
- [ ] **DEPL-03**: Deploy script validates required env vars before deploying (fail-fast on missing vars)
- [ ] **DEPL-04**: Post-deploy health check verifies new revision is serving correctly

### Local Compatibility

- [ ] **LOCL-01**: All Cloud Run changes are guarded by environment detection (no regressions in Docker Compose local dev)
- [ ] **LOCL-02**: Local dev does not require metadata server or Cloud Run-specific auth paths

## v2 Requirements

Deferred to future work. Tracked but not in current roadmap.

### Production Hardening

- **PROD-01**: YAML service manifests replace imperative deploy scripts
- **PROD-02**: Dedicated service accounts per Cloud Run service (least privilege)
- **PROD-03**: Structured JSON logging for Cloud Logging integration
- **PROD-04**: MLflow RequestAuthProvider plugin replaces env var token refresh
- **PROD-05**: Traffic splitting for safe deployments (--no-traffic + verify + shift)
- **PROD-06**: Minimum instances (min=1) for API service to eliminate cold starts

## Out of Scope

| Feature | Reason |
|---------|--------|
| Multi-region deployment | Single region sufficient for hackathon/clinical trial tool |
| Cloud Run service mesh / Envoy sidecar | Overkill for 3-4 services |
| IAP for MLflow | Complicates service-to-service auth unnecessarily |
| Terraform/Pulumi IaC | Shell scripts sufficient for current scale |
| Pub/Sub inter-service communication | Outbox pattern already handles async processing |
| New extraction features | This milestone is deployment-only |
| MLflow auto-scaling | MLflow handles metadata writes sequentially; max-instances=1-2 sufficient |

## Traceability

Which phases cover which requirements. Updated during roadmap creation.

| Requirement | Phase | Phase Name | Status |
|-------------|-------|------------|--------|
| MLFL-01 | Phase 1 | MLflow Decoupling | Pending |
| MLFL-02 | Phase 1 | MLflow Decoupling | Pending |
| MLFL-03 | Phase 1 | MLflow Decoupling | Pending |
| MLFL-04 | Phase 1 | MLflow Decoupling | Pending |
| AUTH-01 | Phase 2 | Service Auth and MLflow Recovery | Pending |
| AUTH-02 | Phase 2 | Service Auth and MLflow Recovery | Pending |
| DEPL-01 | Phase 3 | Deploy Hardening | Pending |
| DEPL-02 | Phase 3 | Deploy Hardening | Pending |
| DEPL-03 | Phase 3 | Deploy Hardening | Pending |
| DEPL-04 | Phase 3 | Deploy Hardening | Pending |
| LOCL-01 | Phase 1 | MLflow Decoupling | Pending |
| LOCL-02 | Phase 1 | MLflow Decoupling | Pending |

**Coverage:**
- v1 requirements: 12 total
- Mapped to phases: 12
- Unmapped: 0

---
*Requirements defined: 2026-02-27*
*Last updated: 2026-02-27 after roadmap creation*

  "context_content": "# Phase 2: Service Auth and MLflow Recovery - Context

**Gathered:** 2026-02-27
**Status:** Ready for planning

<domain>
## Phase Boundary

Fix service-to-service auth so the API can write traces to the MLflow Cloud Run service, and keep tokens fresh across the service lifetime. Requirements: AUTH-01 (MLflow accepts authenticated requests), AUTH-02 (token refreshed before expiry).

**Critical user directive (repeated from Phase 1):** The ultimate goal is the full deployed flow working end-to-end: login → upload PDF → extraction/grounding pipeline → review results. MLflow auth is one piece of this. If other auth or permission issues are discovered during this phase that block the end-to-end flow, they should be addressed — not deferred. The deployment issues report marked Issues 1-8 as \"resolved\" but this hasn't been verified in production.

</domain>

<decisions>
## Implementation Decisions

### Token refresh strategy
- Lazy refresh on expiry: check token age before use, refresh only if expired or within 10-minute buffer
- Cloud Run ID tokens last ~1 hour; refresh when ≤10 minutes remain before expiry
- If metadata server is unreachable during refresh: skip MLflow entirely (trip circuit breaker). MLflow is optional per Phase 1.
- Token refresh should integrate with the existing `_cloud_run_auth.py` module

### Claude's Discretion
- MLflow auth approach: whether to keep IAM-restricted or switch to --allow-unauthenticated (investigate current state first)
- Failure visibility: how to surface auth-specific errors vs relying on Phase 1 circuit breaker
- Whether to use MLflow's RequestAuthProvider plugin vs env var manipulation
- How to structure the token cache (thread-safe singleton, module-level variable, etc.)
- Whether any non-MLflow auth/permission issues need fixing for the end-to-end flow

</decisions>

<specifics>
## Specific Ideas

- The existing `_cloud_run_auth.py` already fetches ID tokens from the metadata server — extend it, don't replace it
- Research should verify whether the MLflow Cloud Run service is deployed with `--allow-unauthenticated` or IAM-restricted — this determines the entire auth approach
- The user cares about the full flow (login, upload, process, review) working — MLflow auth is necessary but not sufficient
- If the researcher discovers other auth/permission blockers (OAuth callback, GCS signing, CORS) that are still broken in production, those should be flagged for inclusion

</specifics>

<deferred>
## Deferred Ideas

- MLflow RequestAuthProvider plugin (more robust than env var, but more complex) — consider for v2
- Dedicated service accounts per Cloud Run service — Phase 3 or later
- MLflow version alignment (v2.19.0 vs v3.9.0) — separate concern

</deferred>

---

*Phase: 02-service-auth-and-mlflow-recovery*
*Context gathered: 2026-02-27*
"
}

### Key Findings

- **Critical discovery:** The MLflow Cloud Run service is deployed with `--allow-unauthenticated` (DEPLOYMENT.md section 4.6a, line 787). This means the reported 403 errors are NOT from Cloud Run IAM rejecting tokens -- they are from MLflow being unreachable (cold start, 503). No token is currently needed for Cloud Run ingress. The token refresh mechanism should still be implemented correctly for future IAM restriction.

- **The existing `_cloud_run_auth.py` is architecturally correct.** It has thread-safe caching, lazy refresh, and Cloud Run environment detection. Only three changes needed: (1) update `_TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN` from 300 to 600 (10 min per user decision), (2) call `configure_mlflow_auth()` from the middleware before MLflow operations, and (3) trip `mlflow_breaker` on metadata server failure.

- **No new dependencies needed.** `google-auth` 2.48.0 is already installed. `pybreaker` and `mlflow_breaker` were added in Phase 1. The `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` env var approach works with the MLflow Python client for Bearer auth header injection.

- **Non-MLflow auth blockers identified:** OAuth callback URL scheme (http vs https), GCS signed URL permissions, CORS origins, and deleted OAuth client IDs are potential end-to-end flow blockers that should be verified during implementation.

- **RequestAuthProvider plugin deferred per user decision.** The plugin provides per-request token refresh but requires entry_points packaging. The env var approach is sufficient for v1.

   116→
   117→### Pattern 1: Lazy Token Refresh Before Use
   118→**What:** Check token age before every MLflow operation. Refresh only when expired or within buffer.
   119→**When to use:** Every code path that uses MLflow (middleware, pipeline trigger, init).
   120→**Example:**
   121→```python
   122→# In _cloud_run_auth.py
   123→_TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN = 600  # 10 minutes per user decision (was 5)
   124→
   125→def configure_mlflow_auth() -> None:
   126→    """Refresh MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN if close to expiry.
   127→
   128→    Safe to call on every request -- no-ops when token is still fresh.
   129→    Trips mlflow_breaker on metadata server failure.
   130→    """
   131→    tracking_uri = os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI")
   132→    if not tracking_uri or not _is_cloud_run():
   133→        return
   134→
   135→    token = get_id_token(tracking_uri)
   136→    if token:
   137→        os.environ["MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN"] = token
   138→    else:
   139→        # Metadata server unreachable -- trip breaker
   140→        from shared.resilience import mlflow_breaker
   141→        try:
   142→            mlflow_breaker.open()
   143→        except Exception:
   144→            pass
   145→```
   146→
   147→### Pattern 2: Token Refresh Integrated with Middleware
   148→**What:** Call `configure_mlflow_auth()` from `_get_mlflow_if_ready()` before creating spans.
   149→**When to use:** MLflow request middleware, before any mlflow.start_span() call.
   150→**Example:**
   151→```python
   152→# In middleware.py
   153→def _get_mlflow_if_ready(path: str) -> Any | None:
   154→    if path in _SKIP_PATHS:
   155→        return None
   156→    if not mlflow_is_available():
   157→        return None
   158→    if not os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI"):
   159→        return None
   160→
   161→    # Refresh token if needed (no-op when fresh or not on Cloud Run)
   162→    try:
   163→        from api_service._cloud_run_auth import configure_mlflow_auth
   164→        configure_mlflow_auth()
   165→    except Exception:
   166→        pass  # Token refresh failure handled by configure_mlflow_auth
   167→
   168→    try:
   169→        import mlflow
   170→        return mlflow
   171→    except ImportError:
   172→        return None
   173→```
   174→
   175→### Anti-Patterns to Avoid
   176→- **Background timer thread for token refresh:** Adds complexity for no benefit. Lazy refresh on use is simpler and achieves the same result. A dedicated refresh thread would also need its own error handling, shutdown logic, and circuit breaker integration. The user decided on lazy refresh -- do not add a timer.
   177→- **Clearing MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI on auth failure:** This would prevent recovery. The token is separate from the URI. The circuit breaker gates access; the URI must stay set.
   178→- **Decoding the JWT to check `exp` claim:** The existing approach of tracking `_token_expiry = now + 3600` is simpler and avoids import dependencies. JWT decoding is unnecessarily complex for this use case.
   179→- **Retrying token refresh in the hot path:** If metadata server is unreachable, trip the breaker immediately. Do not add retry loops to the middleware request path.
